subject: humanities
passage: The siku, a panpipe from the Andes of Bolivia and Peru, is made of cane tubes of different lengths bound together in rows. In its traditional form, the instrument's notes are divided between two separate sets of tubes, each held by a different musician: one set contains every other note of the scale, and the other contains the notes in between. To play a melody, the two musicians must alternate rapidly, so that neither one can perform the whole tune alone. Many Andean musicians describe this interlocking style as an expression of cooperation within a community.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: The siku is made of cane tubes of different lengths bound into rows.
choices.B: Andean musicians favor the siku because it is easier to learn than other pipes.
choices.C: Each siku player performs a separate melody that blends with the other's tune.
choices.D: A traditional siku is built so that two players must share each melody.

explanation.why: Most of the text explains that a traditional siku splits the notes between two musicians, who must alternate so that "neither one can perform the whole tune alone," and the last sentence explains what this shared playing means to musicians. The main idea is that the instrument requires two players to work together on one melody.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This describes how the tubes are made, a detail from the first sentence, not the main point.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says the siku is easy to learn or compares it with other instruments.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The two players do not play separate melodies; they alternate notes of the same melody.
explanation.D: Correct. The text centers on how the siku's notes are split so that two musicians must alternate to play one tune.
